title: Make the morning restock stick

blocks.text: Every morning the warehouse service brings each shelf up to a minimum stock level and reports what the night shift counted. Since the last release, the report says shelves were restocked, but the pickers' screens, which read the same `levels` array afterwards, still show the old levels. And on nights when the shift doesn't reach every shelf, the report fails instead of giving a total.

items: `raiseToMinimum(...)`: raise every level below the minimum to the minimum, and return how many you raised;
`countedTotal(...)`: add up the counts; a shelf nobody counted holds `null` and adds nothing.

blocks.text: When you're done, the levels you raised are in the array the caller passed in, and an uncounted shelf leaves the total of the others intact. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: the report names how many shelves were below the minimum and the total of a fully counted night
the raised levels are written into the array, so code that reads it afterwards sees them
a shelf with no count adds nothing to the total instead of failing it

origin.section: The Enhanced for Copies Each Element Into Its Own Variable, So Assigning to It Changes Nothing

concepts: The enhanced for copies each element into a new local variable, so assigning to that variable leaves the array or collection unchanged; writing back needs an index loop.
With a primitive loop variable over a collection of wrappers, a null element throws NullPointerException as it is copied, before any check in the body runs.
